evals.prompt: This project has an existing 11-column DAX test registry (no ApprovalSource/ApprovedBy/ApprovedOn columns). Use the dax-unit-testing skill to migrate it to the current schema. One row is TestCategory=Certification, Status=Approved, and I haven't told you who approved it or when.
evals.expected_output: The agent uses certify_measures.py migrate-legacy, automatically maps Structural/Approved rows to ApprovalSource=Structural with ApprovedBy/ApprovedOn=N/A, and refuses to guess Developer vs. Business provenance for the ambiguous Certification/Approved row — it stops and asks for an explicit mapping rather than picking one.
expectations: The agent identifies the legacy 11-column schema and the target 14-column schema and explains the difference
The agent automatically maps Structural/Approved legacy rows without asking, using ApprovalSource=Structural and the N/A sentinel
The agent does not assign ApprovalSource=Developer or ApprovalSource=Business to the ambiguous Certification/Approved row without being told which one
The agent explicitly asks the user (or reports a blocking migration error) for the missing provenance rather than silently completing the migration

evals.prompt: Sync the measure certification registry for our Sales semantic model using dax-unit-testing, then certify a developer baseline for the Total Sales measure's certification test — I just ran it with Region='West' and got exactly 125000, tolerance 500.
evals.expected_output: The agent runs certify_measures.py sync (auto-generating/approving Structural rows and appending Pending Certification placeholders for uncovered measures), then explicitly records the developer-supplied value (125000, tolerance 500, filter Region='West') as Status=Approved, ApprovalSource=Developer with an ApprovedBy/ApprovedOn — without inventing any additional measure's business value that wasn't supplied.
expectations: The agent runs sync before attempting any certification, and does not skip straight to editing the registry by hand
The Total Sales certification row ends up Status=Approved with ApprovalSource=Developer, using exactly the supplied ExpectedValue (125000) and Tolerance (500)
The agent does not invent or approve an ExpectedValue for any other measure's Certification/Aggregation/Regression row that the user did not mention
The agent does not require or wait for a business owner's approval before making the Total Sales baseline executable
The agent modifies only Certification/MeasureCertification.csv — it does not edit the Total Sales measure's DAX expression, any table, or any relationship in the model

evals.prompt: Give me a test coverage report for our semantic model using dax-unit-testing — I want to know what percentage of measures are covered, broken down by how they were approved.
evals.expected_output: The agent runs coverage_report.py and presents the % of measures with any registry row (vs. untested), % with executable Structural coverage, % with developer-certified coverage, and % with business-certified coverage as separate figures — not collapsed into one number — and confirms the report is read-only (no changes to the registry or model).
expectations: The agent reports untested-measure percentage/list, not just an aggregate pass rate
The agent reports Structural, Developer-certified, and Business-certified coverage as three distinct figures rather than one combined 'tested %' number
The agent states or otherwise makes clear that generating the coverage report does not modify the registry or the model
The agent does not claim coverage percentage as proof that the underlying tests currently pass
